title: Streaming Player
results: Version 2.0.0 released with a Rust backend and React dashboard
One Docker image for self-hosted deployment
why: Song requests arrive from Twitch chat, YouTube chat and assorted chat bots, and something has to turn them into one queue that plays in OBS. Version 2 swapped v1's Django, Redis, nginx and supervisord for a single Rust container: three fewer things to restart in the middle of a stream.
gains: For a streamer taking requests from Twitch, YouTube and a chat bot at once: one queue, one set of rules, run from chat or the dashboard. When the queue runs dry, your starred songs take over, so dead air stops being part of the show.

lessons: SQLite's plain BEGIN starts as a reader, so a read-then-write queue update could fail with "database is locked" at once; writes now use BEGIN IMMEDIATE.
Since 2025 YouTube's embedded player shows error 153 when the page sends no Referer, so a proxy's no-referrer "security" preset quietly breaks playback.
The first page of YouTube live chat is old chat. It is skipped, or every restart would replay old !sr requests.
subtitle: Song requests, from chat to OBS
description: Twitch, YouTube live chat and chat bots share one song queue. A Rust backend keeps the OBS player, overlay and moderator dashboard in sync.
longDescription: Streaming Player 2.0 is a self-hosted song request system rebuilt with Rust and React. Viewers request songs from Twitch, YouTube live chat or an HTTP API; moderators manage the same queue from a dashboard. Dedicated OBS browser sources provide playback and a transparent now-playing overlay. It replaces the earlier Flask players.
features: Twitch, YouTube live chat and HTTP chat-bot requests
Queue limits, cooldowns, voting and block lists
OBS player and transparent now-playing overlay
Roles, permission points and personal API tokens
